question: Does the 2023 Govantes River macrofauna assessment provide sufficiently reproducible and reusable evidence for any fish occurrence or abundance claims in Vigan, Ilocos Sur?

method.summary: Reviewed Rojas (2023) through the publisher article page and its full-text PDF, including the abstract, methods, searchable results and discussion. Reviewed the January 2023 issue's Editorial Policy PDF for access and reuse terms. The publisher's table pages were not reliably rendered for image inspection in this review, so no table cell values were transcribed. No PDF, table, figure, fish photo or underlying data was retained.
method.samplingAsReported: Three stations were established along Govantes River and three replicates of fish aggregating devices (FADs) were established at each station. Sampling was reported one and two months after FAD establishment. The paper does not state exact collection dates, season, visit-level fish effort, specimen voucher/accession identifiers, or a reproducible fish capture protocol in the reviewed methods.
method.reuseFinding: The January 2023 issue's Editorial Policy describes the journal as open access and says users may read, download, copy, distribute, print, search, or link full-text articles without prior permission. It also says authors transfer copyright to the journal. The reviewed materials do not identify an article-level Creative Commons license or clearly state terms for commercial or derivative reuse of extracted datasets and media. This review retains only attributed bibliographic and factual notes; it does not reproduce tables, figures, photos or raw data and does not approve public app projection.

study.citation: Rojas, C. B. (2023). Assessment of the Diversity of Macrofauna of Govantes River in Vigan City, Ilocos Sur, Philippines. Asian Journal of Biodiversity, 14, 73–87. https://doi.org/10.7828/ajob.v14i1.1547
study.collectionPeriod: Exact calendar dates and season are not reported in the reviewed methods. The paper says sampling occurred one and two months after FAD establishment.
study.habitatContext: The article describes Govantes as a 6.2 km river that reaches the western coast and says the estuary is blocked outside the rainy season. It reports no salinity measurements or sampling-season details that would resolve the conditions during its FAD observations.

reportedTaxonSummary.taxonomicLimit: These are source-reported labels, not independently verified specimen identifications. The figure caption lists 19 labels, while the article reports 20 total taxa and later mentions Lycothrissa crocodillus in the one-area distribution narrative; that name is absent from the caption list. The paper itself recommends further systematics work, including DNA analyses. No name has been silently corrected or accepted as an occurrence assertion.

study.coordinateLimit: The PDF does not identify the datum or CRS for these DMS values. They remain verbatim source-reported study coordinates: no conversion, navigation point, site geometry or river geometry is inferred.
study.tableAccessLimit: Tables 1–3 are present in the publisher PDF but their cells were not available as searchable text, and publisher PDF page screenshots timed out during this review. Counts, station-by-taxon assignments and abundance percentages are therefore not transcribed or independently reconciled.

interpretation: The paper is a historical, FAD-based river assessment with a coastal/estuary connection; it is not evidence of current presence, year-round occurrence, a complete Govantes checklist, catchability, diet, bait suitability, legality, access or water safety.

The study's exact collection dates and voucher/accession trail are not established in the reviewed material, and its authors recommend additional systematic work. Keep its taxon names attributed and unresolved.

The abstract reports 20 macrofauna taxa (13 fish, 6 crustaceans and 1 gastropod), but the Figure 1 caption enumerates only 19 labels. The body later names Lycothrissa crocodillus in a distribution summary without including it in that caption. Do not reconstruct missing abundance cells or treat the total as a verified species checklist.
The DMS points identify the paper's study locations only; the unspecified datum prevents safe coordinate conversion or geometric use.

The issue policy grants broad full-text reading, copying and distribution rights, but no standardized article license or clear extracted-data commercial/derivative terms were found. No table, figure, photo or raw values were reused.

decision.reason: The study is a useful Region I river/estuary research lead, but exact sampling dates, specimen traceability, image-verified abundance tables and a clear article-level reuse license for derivative data use are unavailable. Its stated taxon total also conflicts with its figure caption. Keep the evidence research-only.

nextAction: Continue Region I source discovery across Lower Agno and Lingayen Gulf, rivers, tributaries, reservoirs and estuaries. For this paper, seek author-held sampling dates and voucher crosswalks only if needed; do not digitize the inaccessible table cells or project taxa without source-level validation and a separate rights decision.
